text:
mike: Heads-up: private deployment on a customer T4 node hitting weird latency spikes during continuous batching. Root cause seems related to kernel fallback + KV cache churn. Anyone seen this pattern?

asha: Saw something similar last month but on-prem. Can you drop the profiling trace?

mike: Pasting the perf trace we got from bench-bot (trimmed):

bench-bot: run_id=rb-1816574321
flame_time_ms: 1200
kernel_selection: 
  matmul_small -> gpu_fp16_opt (80%) / cpu_fallback (20%)
  attention_kernel -> gpu_fp16_attn (70%) / fp32_fallback (30%)
memcpy_ms: 240
kv_cache_evictions: 47
avg_tokens_per_batch: 920
avg_wait_ms: 58
token_budget_used_pct: 92%
queue_policy: DELAYED_FILL(timeout=50ms)

lina: Looks like batch formation waits until budget=2048 tokens but they set max_batch_size=16 on a single T4 — latency climb once a few large requests show up. Also KV cache eviction is heavy due to low GPU mem and sticky caching disabled. Suggest setting token_budget_target and lowering batch_size for this private profile.

sam: What about queue_policy? Currently using DELAYED_FILL with 50ms wait. For single GPU you should use IMMEDIATE_WITH_TIMEOUT 10ms or ADAPTIVE to avoid long tails. Example override we used: 

```
batching:
  mode: IMMEDIATE_WITH_TIMEOUT
  timeout_ms: 10
  max_batch_size: 8
  token_budget_target: 512
  kv_cache_retention_ms: 300000
```

asha: Agree. Also kernel selector is flipping to FP16 for most ops but falling back to FP32 for specific head counts and certain attention shapes — that fallback kills latency because of memcpy + recompile penalty. You can force kernel preference with `--prefer-kernel=fp16` or use a per-model kernel selector override, but that can affect numeric parity.

mike: We tested `--prefer-kernel=fp16` on dev: throughput +1.4x but got a small diff on one eval set (higher hallucination rate). Customer needs identical outputs so we can't change kernel semantics without explicit approval. Need a rollback plan.

lina: For strict correctness, use conservative batching + enable KV sticky caching per-connection to avoid eviction thrash. There's an edge build knob `kv.cache.sticky=true` which pins small prefixes in GPU memory; reduces misses but increases memory footprint. For T4 we should also lower `kv_cache_retention_ms` if memory gets tight.

infra-bot: deploy-ci: rolled canary config to private-cluster-3 with IMMEDIATE_WITH_TIMEOUT=10ms, max_batch_size=8, token_budget_target=512, kv.cache.sticky=true. Canary id: canary-181657-can. Status: SUCCESS on 3/3 nodes. Observed p95 latency drop 28%, p50 stable, throughput -6%.

mike: :thumbsup: Thanks. Can we capture these recommended defaults in the private deployment template? Also add automated rollback if perf regresses >10% p50 or >15% p95.

sam: I'll open a PR with a new profile `private-small-gpu` including the config snippet + a helper script to toggle `kv.cache.sticky`. I'll also add a PromRule for `kernel_fallback_rate` and an alert if >5% over 5m.

asha: One more note: for constrained hardware prefer smaller KV retention (~300k ms) + lower token_budget_target per request type (chat vs completion). Chat can get away with token_budget_target=256 for most flows; completions keep 512. We'll draft a tiny runbook for ops.

bench-bot: Saved full trace at https://bench.redwood/internal/trace/1816574321 (flamegraph + kernel-selection log attached).

mike: Nice. Let's sync tomorrow 10am PT to review rollback steps and confirm customer approval before flipping kernels in prod.
